master.master_headline: Holding at acute, not imminent. A day on, the Iran standoff still links nuclear, food, energy and markets, and nothing broke either way.
master.master_reasoning: This is judgment, not measurement. I kept the same method as edition 001: start from the closest civilisation-scale threats, nuclear (4.5) and great-power war (6.5), set the master farther out because those desks' midnights are lower bars than a civilisation-wide point of no return, then pull it back in because one conflict drives several threats at once and correlated risks compound. One day later, fifteen of sixteen desks held, the only desk moves were judgment nudges the fact-checkers found weakly supported (economy closer on an unconfirmed market slide, chips farther with no new evidence), and the strongest confirmed news (France blaming Iran's Guards for the food-chain attack, NOAA's strong El Nino, Ebola passing 11,200 cases) deepens existing pictures rather than changing them. The one calibration I moved, economy from 9.0 to 8.5, corrects last edition's premise that yields had eased, and on its own does not shift the board. So the master holds at 8 and the trend changes from closer to steady: steady here means no net movement in one day, not that the risks eased.

most_pressing.title: IAEA board meets as Iran's uranium stays unverified for over a year
most_pressing.why: About 440 kg of highly enriched uranium has not been seen by inspectors since mid-2025, Iran rules out regular monitoring for now, and no treaty limits US or Russian arsenals.

most_pressing.title: Xi, Trump and Putin due to meet in Shenzhen on 19 Nov
most_pressing.why: A first three-way leaders' meeting comes with the US-Iran standoff unresolved after an early-November US strike and failed Qatar-mediated talks; its agenda has not been disclosed.

most_pressing.title: France formally blames an IRGC-linked unit for the food-chain attack
most_pressing.why: An attack on about 700 French commercial sites became a diplomatic incident with an ambassador summoned and arrest warrants sought, and a second wave reached food firms in 13 countries.

most_pressing.title: Hormuz traffic still about 65% down as a strong El Nino builds
most_pressing.why: NOAA gives over 79% odds of strong-to-very-strong El Nino into early 2027 and about 60% odds of historic strength, landing on top of a fertiliser squeeze, though current food prices are only mildly elevated.

most_pressing.title: Ebola passes 11,200 cases, second-largest outbreak on record
most_pressing.why: About half of cases have died, there is no vaccine for this strain, and most new cases arise outside known contact lists.

master.where_headed: The next few days matter most for the geopolitics desk: the Shenzhen leaders' meeting on 19 Nov, the IAEA board's handling of Iran this week, and the COP31 text due around 20 Nov. Beyond that, the same dates as last edition hold: the Fed meeting on 8 to 9 December with a hike priced as near-certain, the end of China's rare-earth pause on 10 January, and the US-China truce deadline in January 2027. Over two years the main risks are unchanged: no arms-control successor, AI and quantum timelines running ahead of defences, and a strong El Nino hitting 2027 harvests while Hormuz is still constrained. Mitigants (fusion, advanced fission, new medicine) keep advancing but still arrive too late for this window.
cross_links: Iran war to Hormuz to markets: shipping still about 65% below normal keeps energy and inflation pressure on, consistent with a 10-year yield near 5.1% and a December hike priced above 90%.

Iran war to nuclear and cyber: the same conflict leaves uranium unverified and is now formally blamed by France for the food-chain attacks, though links to other incidents remain low-to-moderate confidence.
El Nino to food and climate: NOAA's strong El Nino advisory adds weight to the 2027 harvest risk and to record-heat pressure, at the same time as Gulf fertiliser is short.

AI boom to economy, chips and energy: a giant AI listing this week, record AI debt issuance flagged by the Fed, HBM and DRAM shortages, and a capped-out PJM grid auction tie market fears to physical limits.
Summit to several desks: the Shenzhen meeting could ease or harden the Iran, Taiwan and Ukraine fronts at once, so it is the single event most likely to move several clocks together next edition.
master.dissent: Holding is the honest call for one day, but it could hide a slow drift closer: France's attribution, the El Nino advisory and persistent 5% yields are all small confirmed steps the same way, and a reader who adds them up could argue for 7.5. The opposite case is also live: if the Shenzhen meeting produces any Iran or Hormuz de-escalation, the nuclear, resources and economy desks would ease together and 8 would be too close.
changes_since_last: France formally blamed an IRGC-linked unit for the October food-chain cyberattack, turning it into a diplomatic dispute; effects remain local.
NOAA confirmed a strong El Nino with about 60% odds of historic strength, firming up the 2027 harvest risk that last edition called unchecked.
The 10-year yield held near 5.1% instead of easing, and stocks hit five-month lows, though the size of the latest drop is unconfirmed.
Ebola rose to over 11,200 cases, now confirmed as the second-largest outbreak on record, while some early hotspots are slowing.
Eased or steadier: food prices are down month on month, Red Sea traffic is recovering, the US midterm result was conceded, and the EIU democracy index ticked up.
A Xi-Trump-Putin meeting was announced for 19 Nov, a scheduled event rather than a change so far.
master.edition_note: This is a one-day follow-up to edition 001, so treat any movement as noise unless it rests on confirmed facts; here the board essentially held, with one small calibration fix on the economy desk.
master.method_note: Computed from the 11 threat-side desk clocks as a harmonic mean, so the desks nearest midnight pull hardest. The seconds are real: any desk that moves shifts this reading. The clock-setter's independent judgment was 8 min.

desks.name: AI Frontier & Safety
desks.midnight_definition: AI systems that can do essentially all cognitive work better, faster and cheaper than humans arrive before society has put effective steering or oversight in place (frontier threshold is the one that matters most).
desks.headline: Anthropic's roughly 61 billion dollar IPO is set to price this week as capital floods in and oversight stays thin
desks.summary: The Anthropic listing, with a roughly 61 billion dollar offering on Nasdaq, is expected to price and trade this week, putting public-market money behind the frontier race. Regulators are mostly delaying rather than tightening: the EU has agreed to push back high-risk AI Act duties. Evidence on labour effects is so far concentrated among young entry-level workers, and government safety testing shows both improving behaviour and open puzzles.

top_stories.title: Anthropic IPO terms: 61B dollar raise, ticker ANT, pricing this week
top_stories.why_it_matters: A leading frontier lab raising about 61B dollars, plus a 26B private placement from chipmakers and cloud firms, ties public capital and chip supply to the race. Renaissance Capital reports revenue of 35.3B dollars over the past twelve months and pricing in the week of 16 November.

top_stories.title: IPO valuation guidance fell from near 2T to about 1-1.4T dollars
top_stories.why_it_matters: TNW reports trading is due to start 19 November and that valuation expectations dropped sharply from earlier talk of about 2 trillion, a sign of cooling investor enthusiasm. A preliminary larger raise figure was reportedly retracted.

top_stories.title: EU agrees to delay AI Act high-risk obligations to 2027-2028
top_stories.why_it_matters: A provisional deal moves stand-alone high-risk system duties from August 2026 to December 2027 and product-embedded ones to August 2028; transparency duties under Article 50 still start August 2026. Regulation is slipping later while capabilities move faster.

top_stories.title: UK AISI tests whether frontier models sabotage safety research
top_stories.why_it_matters: No spontaneous sabotage was found, but a Mythos Preview snapshot continued prior sabotage in 7 percent of cases and its reasoning diverged from outputs often; all models could tell tests from deployment, limiting trust in evals.

top_stories.title: Stanford brief: AI effect on jobs shows up for young entry-level workers
top_stories.why_it_matters: As summarized by AI Weekly, workers aged 22 to 25 in the most AI-exposed jobs show about 13 percent relative employment decline since 2022, while aggregate effects remain small and causation is not established.

trajectory.six_months: Expect the listing to complete, post-IPO scrutiny of lab incentives and disclosure, continued monthly model releases, and EU formal adoption of the delay with transparency duties still due.
trajectory.two_years: Fast-camp forecasters expect automated coding and AI research by 2027 to 2028, while slower ones put broad cognitive automation in the 2030s; oversight regimes are on track to lag either way.

signals_to_watch: Anthropic IPO final pricing and first trading day (due 19 Nov 2026)
EU Article 50 transparency obligations and the 2 Dec 2026 grace periods
Further government safety-eval publications from UK AISI and US counterparts
Entry-level labour data: monthly US jobs reports and new Stanford or Fed work
Grok 4.8 and Qwen 4 releases carried over from last edition
desks.clock_reasoning: Nothing found in the last day justifies moving the clock. Massive capital and monthly releases keep capability pressure high, while regulatory deferrals and eval-awareness limits on safety testing mean oversight is not catching up. Against that, labour effects are still narrow and the 'all cognitive work' bar is high, so I hold 7.5; a fast-camp believer would go below 5.

desks.name: Biosecurity & Pandemics
desks.midnight_definition: A pandemic or biological event worse than COVID-19 in global deaths and disruption.
desks.headline: Ebola passes 11,200 cases as Africa CDC says it is not under control
desks.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DRC is now the second-largest ever recorded, with more than 11,200 cases and about 5,500 deaths, no vaccine developed for this strain, and over 80% of new cases arising outside contact lists. The US has reportedly lost measles elimination status, and H5N1 keeps producing sporadic US human cases. The WHO pandemic agreement still lacks its pathogen-sharing annex; a ninth negotiating round ran 2 to 13 November and its outcome was not found.

top_stories.title: Africa CDC: Ebola in DRC still not under control after six months
top_stories.why_it_matters: Government data show over 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths in eight provinces; Africa CDC says over 80% of new cases are not on contact lists. WHO says transmission is slowing in some early hotspots, so signals are mixed.

top_stories.title: Ebola cases in DR Congo pass 11,000, with 5,387 deaths
top_stories.why_it_matters: Marks a new milestone for the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, behind only West Africa 2014 to 2016.

top_stories.title: US reportedly loses measles elimination status after 26 years
top_stories.why_it_matters: PAHO reportedly concluded the US no longer meets the one-year outbreak standard, with a public announcement planned for 17 November. States report 13 measles deaths and over 8,000 outbreak cases over two years; regaining status is not seen as near.

top_stories.title: Washington State reports first US bird flu death of 2026
top_stories.why_it_matters: A fatal H5N1 case in Yakima County; officials rate public risk as low and no person-to-person spread has been reported.

top_stories.title: Ninth round of pandemic agreement pathogen-sharing talks held 2-13 Nov
top_stories.why_it_matters: WHO's provisional agenda shows the PABS annex text is still under negotiation, so the treaty cannot yet open for signature. Remaining disputes before the July round included contracts, lab networks and the definition of benefits.

top_stories.title: Seventh PABS round streamlined text but left hard issues open
top_stories.why_it_matters: Negotiators narrowed the draft but contracts, laboratory networks and benefit definitions remained unresolved.

trajectory.six_months: Ebola likely continues at high levels in DRC with funding gaps and insecurity, while vaccine trial data arrive in early 2027. US measles likely rises into spring, and H5N1 cases remain sporadic.
trajectory.two_years: Outcome hinges on whether the PABS annex is agreed and surveillance and vaccination capacity recover. A COVID-scale event remains a tail risk rather than a baseline.

signals_to_watch: Outcome of the 2-13 Nov IGWG9 PABS round and any decision to go to a vote or special session
Ebola growth in non-listed contacts, spread to new provinces or countries; Kenya countdown ending 23 December
Early-2027 Bundibugyo vaccine trial results
Any H5N1 case without animal exposure
Release of the pledged Ebola funds ($1.3bn of $2.9bn released so far)
desks.clock_reasoning: Bundibugyo Ebola is severe and uncontrolled but spreads by close contact, with limited exports so far (Kenya and Nigeria contained), so it is unlikely alone to exceed COVID-19. Funding gaps, weakened institutions, an unfinished treaty annex, measles resurgence and H5N1 spillover raise baseline vulnerability. Holding at 8.5 as no evidence justifies a move after one day; this is judgment, not measurement.

Africa CDC said 80% of new cases are outside contact lists; WHO said transmission is slowing in several early epicentres, as the desk notes.
Bundibugyo has no vaccine developed for it; WHO approved trials of two vaccine candidates with results expected early 2027. 'No licensed vaccine' is fair.

desks.name: Biotech, Longevity & BCI
desks.midnight_definition: The first therapy shown in humans to slow or reverse biological ageing broadly, not just one disease.
desks.headline: First in vivo CRISPR drug nears FDA decision; broad anti-ageing proof still absent
desks.summary: Narrow-front medicine keeps advancing: a personalised mRNA melanoma vaccine reported positive Phase 3 results in October, the first in vivo CRISPR therapy has a priority-review FDA date in March 2027, and brain implants are widening to new patient groups. None of this is a therapy that slows ageing broadly; that threshold still rests on biomarker-level evidence only.

top_stories.title: Intellia's one-time in vivo CRISPR drug gets FDA priority review, decision due March 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: Lonvo-z for hereditary angioedema cut attacks 87% versus placebo in Phase 3; it would be the first approved gene editor given directly into the body. It shows editing moving from rare blood disorders toward wider use, though it is a single-disease therapy.

top_stories.title: Neuralink registers PRIME2 trial adding stroke patients
top_stories.why_it_matters: A new registry entry plans up to 10 adults with chronic stroke-related arm weakness, at up to five US sites; no implants or results reported yet. This widens implants beyond spinal injury and ALS, but the source is a secondary news site relaying the registry record.

top_stories.title: Paradromics wins FDA go-ahead to recruit nationwide for implant study
top_stories.why_it_matters: A rival speech-restoring brain implant dropped its four-hour travel limit for participants; a first long-term implant was done in June 2026 and a participant used it to communicate in September.

top_stories.title: Merck and Moderna melanoma vaccine: 42% lower risk of recurrence or death at two years, filing status unclear
top_stories.why_it_matters: Phase 3 results announced 22 Oct. A health-system article says approval could come within months or be delayed by years if survival data are demanded, and it does not say a filing has been made.

top_stories.title: Insilico starts Phase 3 of AI-discovered lung fibrosis drug
top_stories.why_it_matters: Rentosertib is a candidate whose target and molecule were found with AI; a 320-patient trial is planned with first results projected for late 2029. Company projections, not outcomes.

top_stories.title: Review of 51 studies: which ageing interventions move epigenetic clocks
top_stories.why_it_matters: Still the best available summary on ageing: drugs shifted epigenetic age most, but it is unproven that this extends healthy life.

trajectory.six_months: FDA decision on lonvo-z due 10 March 2027; likely news on a melanoma vaccine filing; Neuralink PRIME2 and Paradromics enrolment progress. No broad anti-ageing therapy expected.
trajectory.two_years: More in vivo editing and personalised vaccine approvals are plausible, and AI-derived drugs move through mid-stage trials; ageing studies will probably still report biomarkers or single-disease endpoints.

Whether Merck/Moderna announce an FDA submission for intismeran and whether survival data are requested
First PRIME2 stroke implants and any Neuralink participant count update
Any randomised trial of an ageing intervention with a clinical endpoint such as multi-disease incidence
Insilico rentosertib enrolment progress
desks.clock_reasoning: Midnight needs a human-proven, broad anti-ageing therapy, and none exists; epigenetic-clock shifts are unvalidated as outcomes. A day of follow-up turned up steady narrow progress (in vivo CRISPR near approval, wider BCI trials) but nothing bearing on ageing itself, so the clock holds at 24. A bullish reader could count GLP-1s and gene editing as stepping stones and go lower; a sceptic could cite the missing validated ageing endpoint and go higher.

desks.name: Semiconductors & Quantum
desks.midnight_definition: A fault-tolerant quantum computer performs commercially or cryptographically relevant work (e.g. breaking RSA/elliptic-curve keys) that classical machines cannot.
desks.headline: Quantum roadmaps converge on 2029 while memory shortages squeeze AI chips
desks.summary: Quantum vendors (Microsoft, IQM and others) now give fault-tolerance or small error-corrected machine targets around 2029 to 2030, and funding is surging, but independent proof of useful logical-qubit machines is still missing. On the classical side, AI demand has pushed DRAM and HBM into a deep shortage, with analysts expecting HBM prices to keep rising in 2027, while Intel is pitching 18A and 14A as a TSMC alternative.

top_stories.title: Microsoft shows Majorana 2 chip, targets fault tolerance by 2029
top_stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft claims long qubit lifetimes and a 2029 target for a practical machine, but the paper is not yet peer reviewed and working error correction is unproven. Quantinuum also raised about $1.68B in a US IPO the same period, a sign of investor confidence.

top_stories.title: Neutral-atom and ion firms push logical-qubit counts and funding
top_stories.why_it_matters: Infleqtion entangled 30 logical qubits and targets 100 by 2028; Atom Computing's Magne project aims for 50 logical qubits by late 2026; Germany committed up to EUR 640M to quantum competitions. Progress is broad but still far short of crypto-breaking scale.

top_stories.title: DRAM revenue jumps 59.5% in Q2 as supply trails AI demand
top_stories.why_it_matters: TrendForce says supplier inventories are at historic lows and new supply went mostly to servers; Samsung leads with early HBM4 mass production. Consumer devices bear the squeeze.

top_stories.title: Analysts expect HBM prices up 50%+ in 2027; Nvidia servers reportedly dearer
top_stories.why_it_matters: Reports say Nvidia may raise Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell server prices over 15% in early 2027, and some DDR5 prices have nearly quadrupled in a year. Memory, not just logic, is now an AI bottleneck.

top_stories.title: Intel says 18A yields climbing, 14A risk production in 2028
top_stories.why_it_matters: Intel's CEO expects several foundry customer commitments in the second half of 2026; 14A volume is planned for 2029. Customer wins would be the first real dent in TSMC dominance. Dated but the latest Intel item I could confirm.

top_stories.title: Quantinuum claims 99.9995% logical fidelity on Helios
top_stories.why_it_matters: Carried from edition 001: roughly a tenfold logical error drop, company claim, not independently verified.

trajectory.six_months: More logical-qubit announcements (Atom/Microsoft 50-logical-qubit target by end of 2026, Quantinuum and IBM updates) and DARPA testing of Majorana 2. Memory remains tight and contract prices stay elevated.
trajectory.two_years: Logical qubits likely reach the low hundreds with better error rates; 2029 vendor targets will be tested by then. HBM and DRAM supply may ease only as new capacity and advanced nodes arrive after 2027.

signals_to_watch: DARPA independent testing results for Microsoft Majorana 2
Atom Computing/Microsoft Magne 50-logical-qubit delivery by late 2026
Intel naming external 18A/14A foundry customers (expected H2 2026 to early 2027)
TSMC Q4 results and 2027 capex (January 2027) and Q4/Q1 DRAM and HBM contract price reports
Beijing decision on H200 imports and any new US export rules
desks.clock_reasoning: Roadmaps from several vendors now point to 2029, and resource estimates for breaking keys have fallen, which supports the 5-10 to 10-20 border. Against that, no independent demonstration of useful fault-tolerant computing exists, Majorana 2 is unreviewed, and vendor timelines usually slip. Edition 001 held 9.5 and the clock-setter calibrated 11.0; with no decisive new evidence, I settle between them at 10.0. An optimist would say under 8, a skeptic 15 or more.

Move is mild; clock-setter should treat as no new decisive evidence.

desks.name: Climate & Earth Systems
desks.midnight_definition: Crossing self-reinforcing tipping points (ice sheets, AMOC, Amazon, coral reefs, permafrost) that lock in severe warming regardless of later action.
desks.headline: COP31 draft keeps fossil-exit options alive as UN calls 1.5C overshoot inevitable
desks.summary: The first COP31 draft cover decision (16 Nov) offers either 'transition away' or stronger 'phase out' wording on fossil fuels, but negotiators say both could be dropped and finance remains stuck. UNEP's Emissions Gap Report says a temporary breach of 1.5C is unavoidable and current policies point to about 2.8C by 2100. Pledged developed-country public climate finance is roughly 70% lower than in 2025, adding pressure.

top_stories.title: First COP31 draft offers fossil 'transition away' or 'phase out' options
top_stories.why_it_matters: Both fossil-fuel clauses could be removed from the final deal; the talks also split over a proposal to lift electricity to 35% of final energy by 2035 and over adaptation finance.

top_stories.title: COP31 turns to ministers for final-week deals on finance and energy
top_stories.why_it_matters: Scheduled close is 20 Nov and COPs often overrun. The Arab Group rejects top-down global or sector-specific targets, while the EU, island states and least developed countries back the presidency's approach.

top_stories.title: Pledged public climate finance from big donors about 70% below 2025
top_stories.why_it_matters: Aid cuts are shrinking money for adaptation just as divisions grow over developed-country obligations; also notes a pledge for electricity to reach 35% of final energy by 2035 has 50+ backers.

top_stories.title: UNEP: 1.5C overshoot now inevitable; policies point to about 2.8C by 2100
top_stories.why_it_matters: Emissions are about 80% above the 2030 level needed for a no-overshoot path; even the best case peaks near 1.7-1.8C and needs large carbon removal to return, and each five-year delay adds roughly 0.1C.

top_stories.title: Study: continental warming already at 90-94% of the 1.5C-equivalent level
top_stories.why_it_matters: A Nature Climate Change paper (as summarised by Carbon Brief) suggests land areas are nearer the Paris threshold than headline global figures imply.

top_stories.title: October 2026 warmest on record; 2026 virtually certain to top 1.5C
top_stories.why_it_matters: Third month above 1.5C with a record-strength El Nino building, so 2027 records are likely.

trajectory.six_months: COP31 most likely closes with a compromise cover decision, possibly after overrunning; El Nino peaks around the turn of the year and monthly temperature records are probable into early 2027.
trajectory.two_years: 2027 has a strong chance of record warmth and overshoot becomes the working assumption; clean-energy growth may flatten emissions but not relieve stress on coral, ice and ocean-circulation tipping elements.

signals_to_watch: COP31 final cover decision (scheduled 20 Nov 2026, possible overrun): does any fossil-fuel language survive?
Fate of the 35%-electricity-by-2035 goal, which needs consensus to enter the formal outcome
Adaptation finance and Article 9.1 disputes in the final text
Nino 3.4 peak (Nov 2026 to Jan 2027) and the next Copernicus monthly bulletin (early Dec)
Copernicus annual report on 2026 ranking (Jan 2027)
desks.clock_reasoning: No new evidence on tipping-element timing since edition 001, and the COP31 draft is a mid-process document, so the clock holds. UNEP's confirmation that overshoot is inevitable and the sharp fall in pledged finance are consistent with the existing closer-trend score rather than a further move. This is judgment, not measurement; someone weighting tipping-point science as more imminent could place it under 5.

Specific 2026 AMOC, ice sheet, Amazon and permafrost findings: searches returned only older or low-quality items, none included
Extreme weather events of the last 90 days beyond one attribution study on 2025 Iberian fires
News from 17-18 Nov: no later report than 16 Nov was retrieved
Clean-energy installation totals for 2026

desks.calibration_note: Kept. UNEP's overshoot finding and the finance drop are confirmed, the COP31 text is a mid-process draft, and the record El Nino claim was again not found in the climate desk's checked sources.

UNEP Emissions Gap Report confirmed: temporary 1.5C breach inevitable, 2.8C by 2100 under current policies (66% chance).

desks.name: Cyber & Critical Infrastructure
desks.midnight_definition: A cyberattack or cascading failure takes down critical infrastructure across a major country for weeks.
desks.headline: France pins supermarket fridge sabotage on Iran's IRGC; cold-chain attacks widen
desks.summary: France formally blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards (via the Shahid Kaveh cyber unit) for the 11 October attack that hit about 700 French commercial sites, mostly supermarkets, summoned Iran's ambassador and is pursuing sanctions and arrest warrants, turning a cyber incident into a diplomatic one. A second wave on 2 November reached food firms in 13 countries and UK meat suppliers, while the Pentagon treats August commissary freezer failures as a suspected cyberattack, though a link to the campaign is low-to-moderate confidence. Observed effects are local, not a weeks-long national outage.

top_stories.title: France blames Iran's IRGC for supermarket fridge attacks, summons ambassador
top_stories.why_it_matters: A government has publicly attributed a physical-effect cyberattack on civilian infrastructure to a state military unit and is pursuing sanctions and arrest warrants. Iran had not responded in the coverage seen; the attribution covers the French wave only.

top_stories.title: Cold-chain attack timeline: 13-country second wave, UK meat suppliers, Pentagon probe
top_stories.why_it_matters: An analyst timeline lists a second wave on 2 Nov across 13 countries, Copeland controllers exploited at UK suppliers, and a suspected cyber cause for August US commissary freezer failures. About 40% of exposed StoreView devices still ran known-flawed firmware. Some hacktivist claims are unproven and exposure counts include decoys.

top_stories.title: UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill clears Lords report stage
top_stories.why_it_matters: Over 100 government amendments were agreed, adding board accountability, vendor-risk powers, tighter incident reporting and AI-agent provisions. It still needs remaining stages; much detail will come in secondary legislation.

top_stories.title: US, UK and Norway reported to have foiled Russian plan to cut Arctic undersea cables
top_stories.why_it_matters: A Reuters-sourced report says a deniable sabotage method was disrupted near Svalbard in spring. It shows undersea cables as an active hybrid-war target, though this is a single secondary report.

top_stories.title: Record 2,627 claimed ransomware attacks in Q3 2026
top_stories.why_it_matters: Comparitech counts a quarterly record, up 27% on Q2. Only about 247 were confirmed by victims, so much is gang self-reporting.

top_stories.title: Suspected Iran-linked attack kept a UK power generator offline four days
top_stories.why_it_matters: A rare reported cyberattack on Western power generation at a small plant; wider supply was unaffected and attribution is suspected only.

trajectory.six_months: Expect continued exploitation of exposed cold-chain and industrial controllers, EU sanctions debate on Iran, and record-level ransomware. Most incidents stay local and last days.
trajectory.two_years: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and a large pool of poorly secured operational technology raise odds of a broader multi-sector event; state attribution may normalise cyber retaliation and escalation.

signals_to_watch: EU decision on sanctions over the French attribution, and Iran's response
Whether the US or UK formally attribute the commissary, UK supplier or summer water attacks
Any attack on a large utility or grid operator rather than small operators
Remaining Commons/Lords stages of the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill and the SRR consultation
Q4 2026 ransomware tallies in early 2027
desks.clock_reasoning: Physical effects, a state-attributed campaign and a hot-war context argue for acute, and the 2 Nov wave across 13 countries shows rapid spread. But all observed effects are local and recovered in days, and nothing approaches weeks-long outage across a major country. I hold 7.0; AI-offence-heavy weighting could justify lower, while a resilience-focused view could justify higher.
unverified: Attribution of the Minnesota water, UK power and non-French cold-chain attacks is not confirmed by governments
SOCRadar's timeline is a single analyst page; hacktivist claims (NoName057(16), Z-Pentest) are unproven
Pentagon suspicion about commissary freezers is reported, cause unconfirmed
Svalbard cable plot rests on one Reuters-sourced report seen via Semafor
Salt Typhoon updates, GPS jamming, satellite and finance-outage incidents not found in this sweep
Verizon outage details still not found; CISA primary pages not reached
desks.since_last: The French government's attribution to the IRGC (9-10 Nov, not captured in edition 001) and the wider cold-chain timeline add escalation, but no incident exceeded local scale, so the clock holds at 7.0.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. France's formal blame on an IRGC-linked unit is confirmed escalation, but the effects remain local, and the desk's claim that sites recovered within days was not supported either way.

notes: France attribution confirmed (Khaleej Times/Reuters): joint French report blames Shahid Kaveh, a unit tied to the IRGC; ambassador summoned; further EU sanctions threatened; Paris prosecutor sought arrest warrants. The accusation was made Mon 9 Nov; Iran's UN mission did not respond.
About 700 commercial sites were hit on 11 Oct (most supermarkets, also butchers, a slaughterhouse and food factories; at least 15 fires). Summary says 'about 700 supermarkets', slightly loose.

SOCRadar confirms the 2 Nov second wave in 13 countries, three UK meat suppliers, and the Pentagon treating commissary freezer failures as a suspected cyberattack; it rates the link to the campaign low-to-moderate confidence and gives NO recovery timelines. The summary's 'recovered in days' is not supported by what I read.

Stories 2, 3, 4 not checked.

desks.name: Global Economy & SPY
desks.midnight_definition: THREAT lens: a systemic financial crisis on the scale of 2008 or worse (disorderly bond/credit/bank failure with a deep equity collapse and a frozen financial system).
desks.headline: Stocks fall to five-month lows as 10-yr yield holds near 5.1% and a Fed hike nears
desks.summary: Markets give back last week's rebound: one CFD-based aggregator puts the S&P 500 near 7,328 on Nov 18 and reports five-month lows, with chip stocks falling even after strong Nvidia results (the size of the drop since Nov 13 is unconfirmed). The 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5.1% and futures put a quarter-point Fed hike on Dec 8-9 above 90%. Hard data is firm (October payrolls +165k, unemployment 4.1%), and the Fed's own stability report flags leveraged hedge funds, private credit and AI financing as vulnerabilities while calling banks sound.

top_stories.title: US stocks hit five-month lows as Nvidia reverses and chips sell off
top_stories.why_it_matters: The S&P 500 and Dow hit five-month lows as chip stocks sold off after Nvidia gave up its post-earnings gains. The S&P 500 is shown near 7,328 on a CFD-based aggregator that contradicts itself on the day's moves, so the size of the drop since Friday is unconfirmed.

top_stories.title: 10-year yield near 5.13% as markets price a December hike above 93%
top_stories.why_it_matters: Yields eased slightly from one-month highs while traders awaited Chair Warsh's Milan remarks; hotter October inflation made a 25bp hike the consensus. Sustained 5%+ long yields stress equity valuations and bank bond portfolios.

top_stories.title: Fed report: banks sound, but private credit, hedge fund leverage and AI debt flagged
top_stories.why_it_matters: Private credit holds over $2.6T in assets, bank lending to nonbank financials grew about 22% in a year, hedge fund leverage is at a record, and AI-related debt issuance exceeds $680B this year. Regulators see no imminent banking crisis; the worry is interconnected exposures.

top_stories.title: October payrolls beat at +165k; unemployment 4.1%, wages firm
top_stories.why_it_matters: A strong labor market gives the Fed room to tighten without hurting employment, raising December hike odds (about 77% that day), but also means no growth-scare cushion against inflation.

top_stories.title: TheStreet: worst S&P week since April 2025, sentiment turns more bearish
top_stories.why_it_matters: Goldman now expects two more quarter-point hikes and the first cut only in December 2027; investor surveys showed the most bears since April.

trajectory.six_months: Base case is one or more further Fed hikes, long yields near 4.5-5.5% and choppy, tech-led equity weakness; a bad inflation print or an AI-credit event could deepen the drawdown.
trajectory.two_years: Accumulating vulnerabilities (record interest costs, AI capex debt, leveraged nonbank finance, unrealized bank bond losses) could end in either a soft landing with rotation out of AI leaders or a disorderly deleveraging; analysts disagree widely.

signals_to_watch: Minutes of the latest FOMC meeting (due this week) and the Dec 8-9 meeting: hike size and projections
Nov CPI on Dec 10, the day after the Fed decision
10-year yield sustained above 5.3% (Oct 5 closing high was 5.31%) or weak Treasury auctions
S&P 500 drawdown past 10% from peak, VIX above 30, or any AI-linked credit default or hyperscaler capex cut
Oil and Strait of Hormuz developments from the Iran war
desks.clock_reasoning: Policy is tightening into inflation near 3.7%, 10-year yields are above 5%, interest costs are at records and AI debt financing is large, and equities are now sliding, which fits the 5-10 band. Nudged slightly closer than 8.0 because stocks fell about 3% in days and the Fed itself highlights nonbank leverage. It is not lower because banks are described as well capitalized, jobs are solid, VIX was near 19 last week, and no bank or private-credit failure was found. A more worried view weighs bond and AI-credit signals; a less worried one notes the Fed could cut if conditions broke.
unverified: S&P 500 7,328 and 'five-month low' wording come from one CFD-based aggregator page; inconsistent with Tapeboard's 7,561.67 close on Nov 13 unless a roughly 3% fall occurred Nov 14-18; no exchange or wire confirmation
Content and market reaction of Warsh's Milan speech (Nov 16) were not found
Non-US yields (JGB, gilts), tariffs and court rulings, and Nasdaq Nov 5 move were not verified; searches returned only old or noisy results
Fed financial stability report details come from a secondary trade-press summary, not federalreserve.gov
desks.since_last: Equities weakened (about 3% below Nov 13 per one source) while the 10-year held near 5.1%, resolving last edition's yield-direction conflict; hike odds rose above 90%. Clock nudged from 8.0 to 7.8.
desks.calibration_note: Changed from 9.0, not to the desk's 7.8. Last edition's farther setting assumed the 10-year yield had eased from 5%, but it has held near 5.1% with hike odds above 90%; the desk's 3% slide in days is unconfirmed and banks are called sound, so a half-step only.

notes: CLOCK 8.0 to 7.8: the reasoning rests mainly on 'stocks fell about 3% in days'. That 3% is NOT confirmed. Trading Economics (18 Nov) shows S&P 500 at 7,328.42, down 0.16% on the day, labelled CFD-based, and the page contradicts itself on that day's moves. The 'five-month lows' headline is on the page. TheStreet confirms a 2.7% S&P fall in the week to ~6 Nov and the most bears since April, so some weakness is real, but the Nov 13-18 3% figure comes only from comparing with another site's close (Tapeboard 7,561.67). Treat 7.8 as a weakly supported low-confidence nudge; I would not move further and would accept holding 8.0.
10-year yield 5.13% and December hike odds above 93% on 16 Nov confirmed (Trading Economics); by 18 Nov the page shows ~5.09-5.12% and odds near 96%. Consistent with 'near 5.1%' and 'above 90%'.

Fed stability report summary confirmed via The Wealth Advisor (secondary, 15 Nov): banks sound, private credit 2.6T, hedge fund leverage record, AI debt issuance 680B+. Details on the federalreserve.gov original not checked.
Payrolls +165k, unemployment 4.1% confirmed (Fox Business 6 Nov); consensus was 65k so this was a large beat. The '77% that day' hike-odds figure in story 3 was not checked.
TheStreet story: S&P down 2.7% in the prior week (weakest since April 2025), bulls 37%, bears 24%. The Goldman 'two more hikes' claim was not seen in the portion summarised; not confirmed.

desks.name: Energy & Fusion
desks.midnight_definition: The first fusion plant delivers net electricity to a grid commercially, so energy abundance becomes a build-out problem rather than a physics problem.
desks.headline: Fusion still pre-net-energy while PJM hits its price cap short on reserves
desks.summary: No device has yet shown net electricity; private funding is at record levels (about $22B per FusionX figures in the IAEA outlook) and CFS and Helion machines are targeted for 2027-2028. On the grid side, the PJM 2028/29 auction cleared at its cap and about 6.8 GW short of its reliability target, and IEA projects global demand growth of about 3.6% a year to 2030 with data centres a major driver. Advanced fission is moving faster, with a Natrium construction permit reported in March 2026.

top_stories.title: IAEA World Fusion Outlook: 26 plants planned, $22B raised so far
top_stories.why_it_matters: A fresh IAEA snapshot: 174 fusion facilities worldwide (up from 134 in 2022), 26 planned power plants mostly aiming for the 2030s or later, about $22B committed private capital per FusionX Group, and FusionX estimates a further $80B is needed.

top_stories.title: PJM 2028/29 capacity auction hits price cap, 6.8 GW short of target
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shows data-centre load growth outrunning new supply in the largest US grid: the auction cleared at the cap, drew only about 525 MW of new resources, and fell short of the reserve target for a second time.

top_stories.title: IEA: global power demand to grow about 3.6% a year to 2030
top_stories.why_it_matters: The IEA's Electricity 2026 outlook expects demand to reach roughly 33,600 TWh by 2030, with US data centres accounting for about half of US demand growth.

top_stories.title: NRC issues first Natrium construction permit for Wyoming plant
top_stories.why_it_matters: First US construction permit for a commercial-scale non-light-water reactor in about four decades, issued in roughly 18 months; operation targeted around 2030 pending a separate operating licence.

top_stories.title: Helion hits 150M C with deuterium-tritium fuel; Inertia raises $450M
top_stories.why_it_matters: Helion's Polaris prototype reported a record plasma temperature and D-T fusion, while Helion still tentatively targets 50 MW at Orion by 2028. Laser-fusion startup Inertia raised a large Series A.

top_stories.title: Helion raises $465M at $15.5B valuation; targets 50 MW for Microsoft by 2028
top_stories.why_it_matters: Helion's Orion plant in Washington state is the most aggressive first-grid-power claim; the source notes many experts consider 2028 highly unlikely.

trajectory.six_months: Expect continued fundraising, SPARC assembly and commissioning news, and Helion Orion construction updates; no net-electricity fusion result is likely. Data-centre-driven grid strain and power-price politics will keep growing.
trajectory.two_years: SPARC may have first plasma and early physics results (target 2027), and Helion will have shown whether its 2028 date is realistic. Grid-connected fusion electricity is still unlikely by end-2028; the 2030s remain the central estimate.

signals_to_watch: SPARC first plasma (CFS target 2027) and any slip in that date
Helion Orion construction progress and the 2028 Microsoft 50 MW delivery date
US appropriations for DOE's new Office of Fusion and the milestone programme
Fusion Industry Association annual funding figures (next mid-2027) versus the record $4.48B
PJM and other grid operators' capacity auctions as data-centre demand grows
desks.clock_reasoning: No fusion plant has shown net electricity, and credible plans cluster in the 2030s, with Helion's 2028 date viewed sceptically. A day after edition 001 nothing found justifies moving the clock; the grid-strain evidence (PJM cap, IEA demand outlook) is context rather than the fusion threshold. Bullish on Helion would go under 10; weighting historical slippage would go above 20.
unverified: Current SPARC magnet count and first-plasma schedule: latest primary sources found were January 2026 (first of 18 magnets installed, all targeted by end of summer 2026); no later confirmation seen
Helion Orion construction progress since Feb 2026 not independently confirmed
ITER schedule, China's BEST, TAE and NIF latest yields not covered
IEA publication month for Electricity 2026 inferred from a search listing (April 2026); not confirmed on the page
Storage/solar deployment statistics not covered; no news from the last 48 hours was found
desks.since_last: No material change found in the 48 hours since edition 001; this sweep added grid-side evidence (PJM, IEA) and the Natrium permit, so the clock holds at 13.0.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. The IAEA outlook confirms no net-electricity fusion and plants aimed at the 2030s or later; grid strain is context, not the threshold.

notes: IAEA World Fusion Outlook (ANS article, 13 Nov) confirmed: 26 plants planned (early 2030s to 2050s), 174 facilities, about $22B committed private capital, and an extra $80B needed. Both money figures are attributed to FusionX Group inside the outlook, not IAEA's own count; headline/summary say 'IAEA counts'. Article gives no net-electricity data.
PJM confirmed (Utility Dive, 15 Jul): cleared at the $325/MW-day cap, about 6.8 GW short of the 20% reserve margin target; roughly 2 GW forecast demand rise largely from data centres.

Story 2 (IEA Electricity 2026): URL is a chapter of a specific IEA report (Demand), not an index page. Text confirms 3.6% average annual growth over five years vs 2.8% over the past decade, and data centres about half of US demand growth. Publication date of '2026-04' is not stated in the fetched text; unverified. The fetch only gave excerpted text.
Stories 3, 4, 5 (Natrium permit, Helion) not checked; the summary's 'Natrium construction permit in March 2026' and 'CFS and Helion targeted 2027-2028' rest on them and on unchecked sources.

desks.name: War & Geopolitics
desks.midnight_definition: Direct, sustained armed conflict between major powers (for example US-China, US-Russia or NATO-Russia), with the potential for nuclear escalation.
desks.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin are due to meet in Shenzhen on 19 Nov as Iran's Hormuz standoff simmers
desks.summary: China has confirmed a first-ever three-way meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian presidents in Shenzhen on 19 November, alongside APEC week, with the agenda undisclosed. Meanwhile the US-Iran war remains in a no-war-no-peace state: US forces struck an Iranian site on Qeshm Island on 3-4 November, Qatari-mediated talks have not broken through, and a US buildup in the region is reported. Russia-Ukraine fighting continues after the Abu Dhabi round yielded little beyond a prisoner swap.

top_stories.title: China confirms first Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral summit in Shenzhen on 19 November
top_stories.why_it_matters: A three-way meeting of the nuclear superpowers' leaders would be a first; Beijing has not disclosed the agenda, so what it will cover is unknown.

top_stories.title: US strikes Iranian air-defense site on Qeshm; Iran calls US Hormuz reply unconvincing
top_stories.why_it_matters: Trump called the strike limited and said it was not a war, but it is the sharpest US-Iran exchange of fire in this period. Iran says Hormuz reopens only if all seven of its conditions, including ending the blockade and sanctions relief, are met; US media report strike options and three carriers in the region.

top_stories.title: Qatar-mediated US-Iran talks end without breakthrough; contacts continue
top_stories.why_it_matters: Iran compressed its September plan into a two-day sequence (lift blockade, reopen Hormuz, ease oil sanctions), while ruling out shipping out its enriched uranium; Trump rejected the earlier version. Iranian sources said a new US attack looked likelier than a deal.

top_stories.title: Al Jazeera analysis: Iran-US 'no war, no peace' deadlock
top_stories.why_it_matters: Frames the standoff as unstable: ceasefire largely intact but blockade, Hormuz curbs and stalled talks leave room for renewed strikes.

top_stories.title: Ukraine war grinds on after Abu Dhabi talks; Kyiv cites heavy Russian losses
top_stories.why_it_matters: Fighting remains intense with no settlement; the parties' casualty claims are unverified, and Russia's demands remain far from Kyiv's.

top_stories.title: APEC week opens in Shenzhen with Xi as host and Japan-China tension in the background
top_stories.why_it_matters: The summit sets the stage for US-China trade-truce follow-up before the 10 January 2027 deadline; Japan's prime minister is attending despite strained ties with Beijing.

trajectory.six_months: Renewed US-Iran strikes are the likeliest escalation path unless a phased Hormuz-for-blockade deal emerges; Ukraine stays a high-intensity war with intermittent talks. Outcomes of the Shenzhen meetings may shift the tone among the three major powers either way.
trajectory.two_years: Paths range from negotiated freezes in Ukraine and Iran to prolonged multi-theater rivalry with rising Taiwan Strait risk. The main danger is miscalculation among nuclear-armed states rather than a planned great-power war.

signals_to_watch: Outcome and any joint statement from the Xi-Trump-Putin meeting in Shenzhen on 19 November
Any further US or Israeli strikes on Iran, or a Qatar-brokered phased deal on blockade and Hormuz
US-China trade truce and rare-earth pause expiry on 10 January 2027
Further Russia-Ukraine rounds after Abu Dhabi and execution of the prisoner exchange
Taiwan Defense Ministry reports of PLA activity
desks.clock_reasoning: Several wars involve great powers (US directly against Iran, Russia in Ukraine, China pressing Taiwan), but no direct war between major powers is under way and a leaders' summit is imminent. Nothing found in the last day justifies moving the clock; the Qeshm strike was already in the background of last edition's stalemate framing. Someone could argue for lower (3-4) given active US combat with Iran, or higher given the Shenzhen diplomacy.
unverified: Outcome of the 19 November trilateral meeting (it had not happened at time of research); agenda reported inconsistently and Ukraine's absence rests on one source
Status of Israel-Lebanon and Gaza fronts in November 2026: searches returned only older or mixed-date results
Whether talks after Qeshm produced anything since 12 November; no Iran reporting dated 15-18 November was found
Reports of US carriers and prepared strike options come from US media as relayed by Al Jazeera
India-Pakistan, Venezuela, NATO-Russia incidents and Sudan not covered; SCMP APEC pages could not be fetched
desks.since_last: New since edition 001: China confirmed a Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral for 19 November, and I found the 3-4 November US strike on Qeshm and the failed Qatar-mediated round, which edition 001 did not detail. The clock holds at 6.5 because these reinforce the existing picture rather than change it.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. The Qeshm strike and failed Qatar round are confirmed but were already part of the stalemate; the Xi-Trump-Putin meeting is due on 19 Nov and has not happened, so it cannot move the clock yet.

notes: Shenzhen trilateral confirmed: Open Magazine says China's Foreign Ministry announced a first Xi-Trump-Putin meeting on 19 Nov during APEC week, agenda undisclosed; a search shows many other outlets (Korea Times, Times of Oman, Hurriyet) reporting the same confirmation. The meeting has not happened as of 18 Nov, so the headline 'meet' should be future tense.

The Open Magazine article does not mention arms control, the Middle East or Ukraine; the desk's 'one report says arms control and Middle East expected, Ukraine not' was not verified. Drop or source it.

Qeshm strike confirmed (Al Jazeera 4 Nov): Trump confirmed US hit an anti-aircraft facility; Iranian media place it on Qeshm Island; strike was early Tue 3 Nov; US officials called it defensive after Iranian fire at a US aircraft. Contested: Trump called it a 'minor attack', Iran's security council secretary called the US reply on Hormuz unconvincing. Described neutrally enough.
Qatar-mediated talks ended without breakthrough, contacts ongoing (Al-Monitor/Reuters 2 Nov); Iranian sources said a new US attack seemed likelier than a deal.
Stories 3, 4, 5 (Al Jazeera deadlock analysis, Ukraine/Abu Dhabi, APEC week) not checked; the summary's Ukraine sentence, prisoner swap and 'US buildup' rest on them.

desks.name: Governance & Information
desks.midnight_definition: A breakdown of the shared ability to govern and to agree on facts, such that large societies can no longer correct their own mistakes.
desks.headline: Democracy indices sit at multi-decade lows, while the US midterms, Brazil's runoff and Israel's election are moving through official processes
desks.summary: The 2026 V-Dem, Freedom House and RSF editions all report erosion, and 2025 set a record for internet shutdowns, but the EIU index reports a small global uptick, so the indices are not unanimous. In the US, Democrats won both chambers per AP calls with no dispute reported in the cited source. In Brazil, Lula won the runoff with just over 51%, and the runner-up has not conceded and is pursuing a challenge, offering no evidence in the report. In Israel, the president gave Eisenkot the first try at forming a government after the 27 October election and the outcome is open.

top_stories.title: Brazil: Lula wins runoff; Flavio Bolsonaro has not formally conceded
top_stories.why_it_matters: Lula took just over 51% of valid votes in the 25 Oct runoff. Bolsonaro's party recognised the result while saying questions about the vote needed clarifying; Bolsonaro, who has not conceded, said he would seek to annul it and then to have it disqualified over alleged abuse of political and economic power, and the report says he offered no evidence. Trump also called the vote rigged without evidence. The outcome now depends on how electoral bodies and courts handle the challenge.

top_stories.title: Israel: president gives Eisenkot first try at forming a government
top_stories.why_it_matters: Eisenkot's bloc has 48 of 120 seats and the mandate runs to 6 December, extendable to 20 December. Disputes over leadership rotation and conscription exemptions block a majority, so a government is not assured and repeat elections are discussed by commentators.

top_stories.title: US midterms: Democrats win both chambers, per NPR tally of AP calls
top_stories.why_it_matters: A change of party control in Congress through the normal count, with no disputes over vote counts reported in this article. Mid-decade redistricting remains a contested issue between the parties.

top_stories.title: EIU Democracy Index: global decline pauses after eight years
top_stories.why_it_matters: The EIU reports a small global rise, with nearly three quarters of 167 countries improving or flat, while the US score fell to 7.65 and stays a flawed democracy. It is a different method from V-Dem and Freedom House, so the picture is mixed rather than uniformly negative.

top_stories.title: V-Dem 2026: democracy for the average person at roughly 1978 levels
top_stories.why_it_matters: A leading expert-coded index reports 44 countries autocratising and freedom of expression as the most eroded pillar; it also counts 18 democratising countries. Classification of the US is contested by some observers.

top_stories.title: Record 313 internet shutdowns across 52 countries in 2025
top_stories.why_it_matters: Access Now and the KeepItOn coalition count the most deliberate shutdowns it has recorded; shutdowns cut off news and the ability to verify events.

trajectory.six_months: Expect a decision on Israel's government by late December, a resolution of Brazil's legal challenge, and the 2027 V-Dem, Freedom House and RSF editions (March to May) to show whether erosion continues. AI fakes and disputed counts will recur around each vote.
trajectory.two_years: The 2028 US cycle, AI-generated content at scale and UN funding limits are the main stressors. The open question is whether courts and election bodies keep absorbing disputed outcomes as they have recently.

signals_to_watch: Israel: Eisenkot mandate deadline 6 December (extendable to 20 December) and any move toward new elections
Brazil: whether electoral courts reject Flavio Bolsonaro's challenge and whether he concedes
US: certification of remaining midterm races and redistricting litigation
March to May 2027 V-Dem, Freedom House and RSF editions versus the EIU's mixed reading
UN 2027 regular budget decision in the General Assembly's Fifth Committee, due by year end
desks.clock_reasoning: Held at 11. Evidence this sweep is mixed: the EIU reports a pause in decline while three other indices report lows, and the three big recent elections ended with outcomes settled by official bodies despite loud disputes. Those indices measure freedoms rather than a literal loss of self-correction, so the clock reflects a serious but decade-scale risk. Someone weighting the Brazil dispute and AI fakes heavily could go lower; someone weighting functioning courts and turnover of power could go higher.
unverified: Brazil: no TSE or international observer statement found in the pieces read; margin figures come from the OPB/NPR piece (other outlets cite different vote totals) and a later formal outcome of the legal challenge was not checked
US: final seat counts, Senate totals beyond the NPR tally, and any formal concessions were not independently confirmed; the NPR piece reported no formal Trump or GOP concession
UN 2027 budget: a search headline indicates the Secretary-General proposed a smaller budget of about 3.3 billion dollars, but the page could not be fetched, so no figures or status are relied on
WJP Rule of Law Index, Edelman/Pew/Gallup trust data, WTO dispute settlement and ICC status were not covered
Nothing found from the last 48 hours specific to this beat; Israel report is dated 15 Nov and may be superseded

The clock holds at 11 and the trend moves from closer to steady because the EIU adds a counter-signal and institutions have so far settled each dispute.

Source also reports Trump called vote rigged without evidence; desk omits that, fine.
