desks.name: Nuclear & Strategic Weapons
desks.midnight_definition: The first use of a nuclear weapon in war, or an uncontrolled escalation toward large-scale nuclear exchange, which cannot be undone.
desks.headline: IAEA board meets on Iran as no inspector has seen its uranium stockpile for over a year
desks.summary: No treaty has capped US and Russian strategic arsenals since New START lapsed in February 2026, and the Bulletin's Doomsday Clock stands at a record 85 seconds. The IAEA's 13 November report says it cannot locate Iran's roughly 440 kg of near-weapons-grade uranium and cannot rule out diversion, while Iranian clerics are openly debating dropping the no-bomb pledge and nuclear talks with Washington have not begun. North Korea is expanding enrichment capacity, and Russia-NATO nuclear signalling continues at a steady, not sharply rising, level.

top_stories.title: IAEA says Iran's highly enriched uranium still unaccounted for; board meets next
top_stories.why_it_matters: Bloomberg reporting says inspectors have been shut out since the June 2025 strikes, cannot say where about 440 kg of near-weapons-grade uranium is, and Iran rules out regular monitoring for now. The IAEA board meets in Vienna this coming week.
top_stories.source_name: Bloomberg via TNS (Jefferson City News Tribune)

top_stories.title: IAEA voices growing concern over Iran's underground enrichment plant
top_stories.why_it_matters: The confidential report says the agency lacks access to the Isfahan underground site and has lost continuity of knowledge over the stockpile.

top_stories.title: Iranian clerics push to drop the pledge against nuclear weapons
top_stories.why_it_matters: A New York Times report, summarised by Carnegie's Proliferation News, says calls inside Iran to abandon the pledge are growing and public support for a bomb is rising, which would be a major doctrinal shift.

top_stories.title: IAEA reports a second North Korean uranium enrichment building at Yongbyon
top_stories.why_it_matters: Satellite analysis points to a new building that could hold up to 28 centrifuge cascades, plus an operating Kangson site since January, so fissile material production is growing with no inspectors in the country since 2009.

top_stories.title: New START expires; no limits on US and Russian arsenals
top_stories.why_it_matters: The last cap on deployed strategic warheads lapsed. Russia said it would observe the old limits only while the US does; the US wants a broader deal including China. I found no newer verified update on adherence.

top_stories.title: Doomsday Clock set to record 85 seconds to midnight
top_stories.why_it_matters: The Bulletin's closest-ever setting cited the end of New START, stalled dialogue, nuclear coercion talk and states weighing their own weapons.

trajectory.six_months: Expect continued absence of binding US-Russia limits, an IAEA-Iran standoff with possible board censure, and further North Korean fissile-material growth. An explosive test by any state is possible but not the base case.
trajectory.two_years: Without a successor framework, warhead uploads and a three-way US-Russia-China build-up become the default. Iran's nuclear choice and the future of the testing moratorium are the main wildcards.

signals_to_watch: IAEA Board of Governors meeting in Vienna (week of 17 Nov): any resolution on Iran, and whether inspectors regain access to Isfahan
Iranian official statements on NPT membership or the no-weapons pledge
Any US or Russian announcement of warhead uploads or abandoning informal adherence to old New START limits
Any explosive nuclear test or CTBTO detection by US, Russia, China or North Korea
Start (or not) of US-Iran nuclear negotiations; formal US-Russia-China arms talks
desks.clock_reasoning: I hold 4.5 minutes. The structural guardrails are gone and Iran's material is unverified with its internal debate shifting, but fighting wound down in April, there is no sign of imminent use, and nothing in the last 48 hours materially changes the picture. Lower would need explicit deployment-linked threats, a test or an Iranian weaponisation signal; higher would need a working successor framework or restored inspections. This is my own judgment, not a measurement.
unverified: Whether the US and Russia still informally observe former New START limits as of November 2026; the latest sources I saw were from February.
Whether the US has conducted or scheduled an explosive test; searches returned only 2025 and early-2026 items.
Exact dates of the IAEA board meeting and any draft resolution.

Current Russia-Ukraine nuclear rhetoric: search returned mostly older Medvedev items, nothing dated within the past month except false nuclear alerts sent through alert apps around 1 Nov (secondhand via Carnegie).
Golden Dome, hypersonics, India-Pakistan and Saudi proliferation not covered this sweep; armscontrol.org news page failed to fetch.
desks.since_last: Follow-up confirmed the Iran/IAEA picture with Bloomberg detail (about 440 kg of HEU unlocated, board meeting this week) and added Iranian bomb-pledge debate and North Korea's enrichment expansion; no event justified moving the clock, so it holds at 4.5.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. The fact-checker passed this desk in full: about 440 kg of Iranian highly enriched uranium is still unverified with inspectors out since mid-2025 and no arms-control caps, but there is still no sign of imminent use.

notes: Checked Iran/IAEA (Tribune/Bloomberg 15 Nov, The National 13 Nov) and Carnegie newsletter (5 Nov): all exist and match.

Tribune: about 441 kg HEU unverified, inspectors out since June 2025, IAEA says cannot conclude no diversion, board meets next week, Iran rules out regular monitoring now, talks not started. The National says 'more than 400 kg', so the ~440 kg figure is sourced to the Tribune article only.
Clerics debate: the Carnegie page is a newsletter linking an NYT piece; confirms mainstream debate on dropping the pledge. The page says nothing on Washington talks status (that is from the Tribune).
Nuclear stories 3 (Yongbyon), 4 (New START), 5 (Doomsday Clock 85 seconds) not checked. Clock hold at 4.5 is stated as judgment; headline is measured, not sensational.

desks.name: Food, Water & Resources
desks.midnight_definition: Simultaneous failure of several major food-producing regions, or a resource shock, that causes mass hunger across multiple continents.
desks.headline: Hormuz still choked while a possibly record-strength El Nino builds toward the 2027 harvests
desks.summary: Hormuz traffic remains about 65 percent below pre-war levels with tanker attacks continuing (seven tanker incidents in the latest UKMTO week), though crude exports and oil supply have partly recovered. NOAA now reports a strong El Nino (Nino 3.4 about +2.5C) with over 79 percent odds of strong-to-very-strong conditions through early 2027 and about a 60 percent chance of historic strength, landing on top of a fertiliser squeeze. Headline food prices are only mildly elevated (FAO 133.9) and Red Sea traffic is recovering, so the risk is 2027 yields, not current shortage.

top_stories.title: Hormuz traffic still about 65% below pre-war; seven tanker attacks in latest UKMTO week
top_stories.why_it_matters: UKMTO logged eight incidents in its latest week, seven on tankers. IEA says Gulf oil exports reached 18.4 mb/d in October, still 26% under pre-war, with a projected Q4 supply surplus of 1.7 mb/d. Related headlines on the page point to further tanker attacks on 16 November, which the article itself does not cover.

top_stories.title: NOAA: strong El Nino in place, over 79% odds it stays strong into early 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: Niño 3.4 anomaly near +2.5C and a roughly 60% chance of historic strength raise risks for crops in Australia, India, Southeast Asia and Brazil. Next update is 10 December.

top_stories.title: FAO food price index confirmed: 133.9 in October, down 1.2%, still 5.9% up on year
top_stories.why_it_matters: Confirmed on FAO's own page: cereals fell 4.5% and sugar rose 6.6%, vegetable oils stay very high at 199.2. Prices are lagging the fertiliser and weather shocks.

top_stories.title: Hunger Hotspots: Sudan, South Sudan, Yemen, Gaza, Nigeria, Somalia at highest concern
top_stories.why_it_matters: Famine risk covers 14 areas of Darfur and Kordofan, with about 200,000 people projected in IPC Phase 5; DR Congo is a very-high-concern hotspot with Ebola complicating food access. Data cutoff was 5 June, so it predates later alerts.

top_stories.title: Red Sea recovery continues: Suez transits at post-crisis high, no attacks since August
top_stories.why_it_matters: Suez October transits were about 34% below pre-crisis and Bab el Mandeb about 46% below, but both are rising. A large unexplained blast near Bab el Mandeb on 6 November keeps the risk live.

top_stories.title: US finalises Colorado River 2027-28 rules with 1.25 million acre-foot Lower Basin cuts
top_stories.why_it_matters: Sets the first post-2026 water regime for a basin feeding major farm regions, with Lake Powell protected near 3,510 ft and the final 2027 release set in April.

trajectory.six_months: Fertiliser cost and availability will shape 2027 planting just as El Niño impacts on Southern Hemisphere and Asian crops emerge. Sudan and other hotspots likely worsen without funding.
trajectory.two_years: If Hormuz stays impaired and El Niño cuts yields in several regions, a multi-continent food price spike is plausible; if shipping normalises, the system probably absorbs it with regional hunger increases.

signals_to_watch: NOAA ENSO update on 2026-12-10 and Australian, Indian and Brazilian crop estimates
FAO Food Price Index in early December and January, especially vegetable oils and rice
Weekly UKMTO Hormuz transit counts and tanker attacks
China rare-earth suspension expiry around 2027-01-10
Any new IPC famine classification in Sudan
desks.clock_reasoning: Midnight needs several breadbaskets failing together or a shock causing mass hunger across continents. Overlapping drivers (Hormuz, fertiliser, a possibly historic El Niño) are real, but prices are only moderately elevated, oil is in surplus and Red Sea traffic is recovering, so nothing in the last day justifies a move. Someone could set it closer by weighting El Niño plus fertiliser effects on 2027 yields, or farther if Hormuz normalises.
unverified: El Niño figures come from a local TV report relaying NOAA; not checked on the NOAA CPC page itself.
Hormuz 65% figure combines AIS data with US-reported transits that UKMTO says it could not verify.
Latest fertiliser (urea) price levels for November not confirmed; only older Fertilizer Daily headlines seen.
Gaza and DR Congo current IPC status not confirmed beyond the June Hunger Hotspots report.
Panama Canal status, India aquifers, Tehran water and fisheries not researched.
Lloyd's List brief is internally inconsistent on whether Houthi attacks have resumed.
desks.since_last: Held at 6.0. The FAO October index was verified on fao.org, NOAA's strong El Niño and Red Sea recovery were added, and attacks on Hormuz tankers continued on 16 November; none of this changes the picture materially.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. NOAA's strong El Nino and Hormuz traffic about 65% down are now confirmed, but historic strength is only a probability, food prices are mild and oil is in surplus, and the new tanker-attack claim overreached.

notes: gCaptain article is dated 13 Nov, not 16 Nov. It confirms ~65% below pre-war traffic, 8 UKMTO incidents (7 tankers), IEA Gulf exports 18.4 mb/d (26% below pre-war), Q4 surplus 1.7 mb/d. The '16 November, two more tankers hit' claim appears only in related-article teasers on that page, not in the article; headline/summary overreach on that.

NOAA via Fox10 (12 Nov): El Nino advisory, Nino 3.4 +2.5C, over 79% chance of strong-to-very-strong through JFM 2027, and about 60% chance of reaching historic strength. 'Record-class' in the headline is a probability, not an observation; reworded.
FAO Food Price Index 133.9 for October, down 1.2% m/m, up 5.9% y/y confirmed on fao.org (page is a live index page, so it will change).
Stories 3 (Hunger Hotspots PDF), 4 (Lloyd's List), 5 (Colorado River) not checked. Clock hold at 6.0 is judgment; no clock-moving claim rests on the unsupported 16 Nov detail.

desks.name: Robotics & Autonomy
desks.midnight_definition: General-purpose robots (humanoid or otherwise) doing ordinary physical work at scale more cheaply than human labour, across many job types rather than in a few controlled niches.
desks.headline: Autonomy scales in narrow niches (trucks, taxis) while humanoid AI still fails fine tasks
desks.summary: Narrow autonomy keeps scaling: Aurora has passed 500,000 driverless truck miles and is building trucks at a growing rate though about six weeks behind plan, Zoox is extending its purpose-built robotaxi testing to more cities, and Tesla and Waymo continue expansion. Robot foundation models are improving (Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2), but published numbers show weak results on some fine manipulation tasks, and humanoid production is still small. Nothing in the last day changes the picture from edition 001.

top_stories.title: Aurora passes 500,000 driverless miles; production ramp about six weeks behind plan
top_stories.why_it_matters: Driverless trucking is real and growing (more than 20 trucks built, target above 200 by end of February, over 1,000 by end of 2027), yet revenue is tiny at about 3 million dollars in Q3 (about 9 million expected for 2026) and the production ramp is about six weeks behind plan.

top_stories.title: Zoox extends robotaxi testing to Atlanta, following Austin and Miami
top_stories.why_it_matters: Amazon's steering-wheel-free robotaxi is open to the public in Las Vegas and in an early-rider program in San Francisco; Atlanta rides are limited to employees and guests for now, and fleet size is undisclosed.

top_stories.title: Google DeepMind releases Gemini Robotics 2 for whole-body humanoid control
top_stories.why_it_matters: A single model can drive a humanoid's legs and hands and adapt to a new robot body from under 200 examples, but reported success rates were 92% for unscrewing a bulb and only about 40% for sealing a bag, so general dexterity is not solved.

top_stories.title: Humanoid deployments: Figure at BMW, Agility totes, Unitree unit costs down 70%
top_stories.why_it_matters: Reported figures include Figure units contributing to over 30,000 BMW vehicles, over 100,000 totes moved by Agility's Digit, and Unitree prices falling from about 85K to 25K dollars with roughly 60% gross margin in its IPO filing; the cost curve is the key variable for midnight. Secondary source, date approximate.

top_stories.title: Tesla starts Optimus production at Fremont, calls ramp slow and uneven
top_stories.why_it_matters: First production humanoids from the largest would-be volume maker, though the company concedes the robot still needs significant work. Carried from edition 001.

top_stories.title: Waymo reaches 500,000 paid driverless rides a week in 10 US cities
top_stories.why_it_matters: Still the newest official Waymo volume figure I could find; the stated goal is a million a week by end of 2026.

trajectory.six_months: Aurora should show whether it reaches 200 trucks by end of February; Zoox and Waymo keep adding cities; humanoid output stays in the hundreds to low thousands per maker.
trajectory.two_years: Driverless trucks and robotaxis become routine on major corridors in the US and China, and humanoids reach tens of thousands of units in pilots, with cost-competitive general labour still unlikely.

signals_to_watch: Aurora truck count versus 20 per week by early December and over 200 by end of February
Waymo's next weekly-ride figure against its 1 million per week year-end goal
Tesla Q4 results on Optimus output and unsupervised robotaxi timing
Zoox opening Atlanta, Austin and Miami to public riders
Gemini Robotics 2 and Physical Intelligence success rates on fine manipulation in real deployments
desks.clock_reasoning: Narrow autonomy is scaling, but midnight needs general-purpose robots doing varied work more cheaply than people, and the best published robot model results still fail often on fine tasks. Falling humanoid unit prices and early trucking deployment are real, but no new evidence moved the estimate in one day, so I hold 13. Someone weighting Chinese hardware cost curves could argue for under 10; someone weighting dexterity failure rates could argue for 20 or more.
unverified: Waymo's current (Nov 2026) weekly rides and fleet size: searches returned only the March 2026 figure and older material
Tesla robotaxi fleet size: search headlines suggest conflicting reports (shrinking versus growing) that I did not open
China regulatory pause of May 2026 and Apollo Go status not checked this edition
Humanoid cost and deployment numbers come from a secondary aggregator without a clear date
Amazon robot count and Figure 03 and Physical Intelligence updates not confirmed
desks.since_last: Added Aurora, Zoox and Gemini Robotics 2 coverage from open threads; no new event in the last day changed the picture, so the clock holds at 13.0 and trend moves from closer to steady.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. Aurora's driverless miles and Zoox testing are confirmed, but published robot results still fail often on fine tasks and humanoids remain at small volume.

notes: Aurora SEC letter (28 Oct) confirmed: 500,000+ driverless miles, 20+ trucks, 200 by end Feb, 1,000+ by end 2027, Q3 revenue $3M, ramp ~6 weeks behind. The letter gives ~$9M 2026 revenue but does not state a prior outlook, so 'cuts 2026 revenue outlook' is unsupported; title corrected.
Zoox (13 Nov) confirmed as testing only in Atlanta (employees, friends and family; public waitlist planned); summary phrase 'spreading to more cities' is fine but should not imply public service.
Gemini Robotics 2 (TNW, 30 Jul): published fine-task rates are mixed, 92% light bulb, 44% trash bag, 40% ziplock, so 'weak on fine manipulation' is supported for some tasks.
Stories 3 (humanoid deployments/Unitree 70%), 4 (Tesla Optimus), 5 (Waymo 500k rides) not checked; the summary's Tesla/Waymo lines rest on them. Clock hold at 13 is judgment.

desks.name: Global Health & Demographics
desks.midnight_definition: Demographic and social strain (ageing, shrinking workforces, health-funding collapse) becomes so severe that major societies can no longer sustain their pensions, health systems and workforce.
desks.headline: Aid fell a record 23% in 2025 as WHO warns health gains are reversing
desks.summary: Official development assistance dropped by nearly a quarter in 2025, the largest fall on record, and aid agencies warn of further pressure. WHO's 2026 statistics report says the world is off track on health goals, with some areas reversing, while a new economics paper argues global fertility is already near replacement level and world population may peak decades earlier than the UN expects (a single paper, contested). Pension strain is visible in Europe, but nothing in the last 48 hours changed the picture.

top_stories.title: Global aid fell 23.1% in 2025, the biggest drop on record
top_stories.why_it_matters: Preliminary OECD data show the US drove roughly three-quarters of the fall, with Germany, France, the UK and Japan also cutting; humanitarian aid fell about 36%. The Global Fund and Gavi face critical shortfalls.

top_stories.title: OECD confirms largest annual aid drop in its history
top_stories.why_it_matters: The OECD's own release puts the 2025 real-terms fall at 23.1% for DAC members and associates, the primary-source confirmation of the trend behind health-funding strain.

top_stories.title: WHO: world off track on health goals, gains reversing in places
top_stories.why_it_matters: Malaria incidence is up 8.5% since 2015 and coverage progress has slowed, though new HIV infections are down 40% since 2010. WHO calls the financing situation a worsening crisis and notes most countries report death data late.

top_stories.title: Paper: world fertility near 2.2, population peak around 2056
top_stories.why_it_matters: Two economists argue the global rate is about at replacement and population could peak near 9 billion, about three decades before the UN's central projection. This is a contested projection, not official UN data.

top_stories.title: French parliament voted to freeze 2023 pension age rise
top_stories.why_it_matters: The Assembly voted to hold the retirement age at 62 years 9 months until after the 2027 election, at a stated cost of about 1.9 billion euros in 2027. It shows how hard pension adjustment is politically; this is older news and its current status was not confirmed.

trajectory.six_months: Expect more record-low birth figures from East Asia and early signs of aid-cut effects in immunization and disease data; donor budgets for 2027 will show whether cuts deepen.
trajectory.two_years: Aid is projected to decline further in 2026, so measurable health setbacks in low-income countries are likely, while ageing pushes pension and retirement-age fights across Europe and Asia.

signals_to_watch: OECD final 2025 ODA data and 2027 donor budget decisions
China, Japan and Korea 2026 birth counts (early 2027)
Gavi and Global Fund funding gaps and any programme cutbacks
UN World Population Prospects update vs the 2056 peak claim
European pension rules ahead of France's 2027 election
desks.clock_reasoning: Demographic decline is near-certain but pension and health-system failure is gradual and policy-dependent, so the 10 to 20 band fits. Record aid cuts and WHO's reversal warnings keep it on the closer side at 17. No evidence this run justified a move; someone who expects faster health-system damage from aid cuts, or who trusts the earlier population peak, would set it lower.
unverified: Whether France's pension suspension was finalised and its current status in late 2026 (only the Nov 2025 Assembly vote was seen).
Fetch of the Anadolu piece on the French Senate failed.
Total ODA dollar amount and health-specific aid totals were not retrieved.
Fertility paper figures are one outlet's summary of a working paper, not peer-reviewed or UN data.
Not covered: life expectancy figure, poverty, loneliness, housing, China and Japan pension news; no fresh news from the last 48 hours was found.
desks.since_last: No material change in the last day; this sweep added aid-cut, WHO statistics and fertility-projection context, so the clock holds at 17.0.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. The record aid fall and WHO's warning are confirmed, but they play out over decades and depend on policy; the early-population-peak paper is single and contested.

notes: Health Policy Watch (10 Apr): ODA fell 23.1% in real terms in 2025, most severe on record; US about three-quarters of the fall (US cut ~57%); humanitarian aid -36%; Global Fund and Gavi warned. Confirmed.

OECD press release exists and confirms 23.1% fall and 'largest annual drop in history'. Its 2026 projection was not visible in the portion I read (page truncated), so summary's 'OECD projects a further decline in 2026' is not confirmed by me.
WHO World Health Statistics 2026 (13 May, News-Medical): off track on all health-related SDGs, progress slowing and in some areas reversing. Confirmed; 'gains reversing' is in places only.

Stories 3 (fertility paper) and 4 (France pensions, Nov 2025, over a year old) not checked. The fertility/peak 2056 claim in summary is an unreviewed-sounding economics paper per desk; flag as contested. Clock hold at 17 is judgment.

desks.name: Space
desks.midnight_definition: Permanent human presence beyond Earth becomes self-sustaining in practice: routine, cheap, fully reusable heavy lift plus a crewed base that persists.
desks.headline: Starship's ship catch stands, but refuelling is still unproven and orbit grows more contested
desks.summary: Starship Flight 15 returned its ship to the tower about 22.5 hours after launch, while the booster aborted its catch and splashed down in the Gulf. Orbital refuelling, needed for any lunar landing, has no demonstration date yet, and NASA still targets a first crewed landing on Artemis IV in 2028 with Blue Moon as a possible fallback. On the threat side, analysts and war-game reports describe a growing risk from Russian orbital anti-satellite and nuclear-in-orbit concepts, with US response options judged thin.

top_stories.title: After Flight 15: ship caught, refuelling and reflight still ahead
top_stories.why_it_matters: SpaceX says double catches become standard, but no rapid reflight of either stage has been shown and the first refuelling test has no firm date. Tanker visits needed per lunar mission are estimated from six or eight up to 22.

top_stories.title: Artemis IV 2028 landing depends on Starship crew cabin; Blue Moon is fallback
top_stories.why_it_matters: SpaceX reportedly aims to finish a full-scale crew cabin ground prototype by end of 2026; if Ship is late, NASA may turn to Blue Origin's lander.

top_stories.title: Analyst: Russia treats destroying satellites as part of nuclear war planning
top_stories.why_it_matters: An FPRI paper argues Russia has long viewed destroying US satellites as part of nuclear war planning and may be exploring nuclear-armed satellites; the paper says much of this is inference from Russian military writings.

top_stories.title: War-game report: US lacks response options to a nuclear weapon in orbit
top_stories.why_it_matters: A think-tank study found the US unprepared in all four tabletop scenarios, with weak detection and attribution and no tested recovery plan after an orbital detonation.

top_stories.title: China's Mengzhou 1 still listed as a late-2026 debut on Long March 10A
top_stories.why_it_matters: The capsule's first orbital flight and Tiangong docking is the next marker for China's 2030 crewed landing goal; reference sources show it as planned, not yet flown.

trajectory.six_months: Expect investigation of the booster abort, a Flight 16, possibly the first propellant transfer demonstration, and a Mengzhou 1 attempt.
trajectory.two_years: Artemis III orbital rehearsal in 2027 and a landing attempt around Artemis IV in 2028 are the milestones; a persistent crewed base is still beyond this window.

signals_to_watch: First Starship ship-to-ship propellant transfer date
Flight 16 timing and whether a booster catch succeeds
Mengzhou 1 / Long March 10A launch and Tiangong docking
SpaceX crew cabin ground prototype by end of 2026
Any Russian co-orbital or nuclear-in-orbit developments
desks.clock_reasoning: Nothing found in the last day changes the picture: a ship has been caught, but cheap routine reusable heavy lift, refuelling and a persistent base remain undemonstrated. First landing is targeted for 2028 and China's for 2030, so roughly a decade away. This is judgment; someone confident in 2027 refuelling could set it nearer 8 minutes, while someone weighting orbital conflict risk could set it farther.
unverified: FAA mishap investigation status for Flight 15 (not stated in sources; search surfaced only Flight 12 coverage)
Whether Mengzhou 1 has flown (reference page may be out of date)
Space weather and solar cycle 25 current status (search returned only archive pages, not read)
Commercial stations (Vast Haven-1 date) and planetary defence not confirmed; results were old
Moscow Times result dated 2026 actually described a 2021 Russian ASAT test and was discarded
desks.since_last: Followed up Flight 15 aftermath (no new FAA, Flight 16 or refuelling dates found) and added the ASAT threat-side gap from August and September 2026 sources. Clock held at 14.0 because nothing new in 24 hours moves it.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. The desk passed in full; the ship catch stands, refuelling still has no date, and a crewed landing is 2028 at the earliest.

notes: Space.com (Flight 15 aftermath) confirmed: launch 13 Nov, ship caught 14 Nov about 22.5 h after liftoff, first ship catch; booster aborted its catch after a low-fuel alarm and splashed in the Gulf; no refuelling date (article says likely 'relatively soon'); tanker estimates 6 to 8 (Musk) up to 22 (outsiders); Artemis IV 2028, Blue Moon possible fallback. Stories 0 and 1 share one URL, which is acceptable but they are not independent sources.

FPRI (6 Aug, Aaron Stein): presents Russian view as long-standing and largely inferential; desk wording 'analyst' is fair, but it is an assessment, not a stated Russian policy. Military Times (16 Sep) covers an American Foreign Policy Council report from April 2026 based on two 2025 war games; confirmed that the US 'appears to lack response options' in one scenario.
Story 4 (Wikipedia, Mengzhou 1) not checked; Wikipedia is a weak source for a launch date. China 2030 landing claim not checked. Clock hold at 14 is judgment.

desks.name: Natural Hazards & Wildcards
desks.midnight_definition: A natural or out-of-the-blue event (supervolcanic eruption, impactor, extreme solar storm, mega-quake) with global consequences that nobody was positioned for.
desks.headline: Campi Flegrei's M4.7 injured 21 in July; no global-scale natural threat found
desks.summary: Hazard activity is elevated but regional: Campi Flegrei produced its strongest quake of the unrest on 31 July, a deep M7.1 hit eastern Indonesia on 16 November, and the Sun is delivering only minor geomagnetic storms. Nothing found points to an imminent global-scale event.

top_stories.title: Campi Flegrei M4.7 quake injures 21 and damages buildings near Naples
top_stories.why_it_matters: The strongest shock of the current unrest struck at about 3 km depth, hurt 21 people, evacuated 18 families, damaged churches and homes, and closed Pozzuoli port. It shows the caldera can do real local damage; the page gave no alert level or uplift figure.

top_stories.title: M7.1 quake at 115 km depth off Maluku Tenggara, Indonesia
top_stories.why_it_matters: A major but deep event (BMKG data) in the Banda Sea region, with no inhabitants estimated within 100 km; the page gives no tsunami assessment. Depth limits surface shaking.

top_stories.title: Coronal-hole stream drives G1 storm; radiation-belt electrons run high
top_stories.why_it_matters: Minor G1 storming on 7-8 Nov, strong electron flux at geostationary orbit (internal charging risk for satellites), and seven M-class flares from one sunspot region, none Earth-directed. NOAA outlook lists more G1 periods on 17-18 Nov, 27-28 Nov and 4-5 Dec.

top_stories.title: Strong shallow M6.4 quake hits Santa Cruz Islands, Solomon Islands
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shallow (17 km) event with USGS Green alert, meaning low expected casualties, though local construction is vulnerable. Regional, routine for the Ring of Fire.

top_stories.title: Shallow M7.0 quake on Xizang-Qinghai border (carried from edition 001)
top_stories.why_it_matters: Strong shallow quake in a remote region with vulnerable buildings; regional scale only.

trajectory.six_months: Expect continued Campi Flegrei quakes with a real chance of further M4+ events, routine global M6-7 quakes, and recurring G1-G2 storms from coronal holes as the cycle declines.
trajectory.two_years: Solar flare intensity should fall but extreme storms stay possible; Campi Flegrei unrest could plateau or escalate; Iceland's Reykjanes system is likely to erupt again, with regional rather than global effect.

desks.clock_reasoning: Global-scale natural catastrophes are rare and none of the indicators checked is at alarm level, so the clock holds in the live-but-slow range. The Campi Flegrei M4.7 is a meaningful local escalation but not a global threat, and it was already in the background of edition 001. Someone could argue lower for grid and satellite fragility, or higher given long base rates; coverage this run was thin.

notes: Euronews (31 Jul) confirmed: M4.7 at about 3 km depth, 21 injured (two seriously), 18 families evacuated, Pozzuoli port closed. URL slug says 'injuring four' but body says 21; fine.

Indonesia M7.1 page (16 Nov 21:11 UTC, BMKG) confirmed: depth 115 km, near Maluku Tenggara. The page does not state a tsunami assessment either way, so 'reported no tsunami threat' is not supported; reworded. It is a tsunami-SMS aggregator, secondary.

Watchers (11 Nov) confirmed: G1 storm peaked 7 to 8 Nov, only minor level; high-energy electron flux elevated at geosynchronous orbit through about 13 Nov. Summary 'only minor geomagnetic storms' fine.

Stories 3 (Solomon M6.4) and 4 (Xizang M7.0, carried from edition 001) not checked. Headline leads with a July event, 3.5 months old, and calls it the strongest of the unrest: Euronews says strongest in years. Clock 42 is judgment; not sensational.
